system.name: RoboCerebra
system.one_liner: A large-scale simulation benchmark for System 2 reasoning in long-horizon robotic manipulation, with trajectories about 6 times longer than earlier benchmarks.

content.variant_note: three unequal tiles: a construction pipeline strip on top, a ten-frame task filmstrip with four challenge cards, and a bar chart with a headline multiplier
content.argues: RoboCerebra tasks run about 6 times longer than earlier benchmarks and need memory, planning and recovery, and the data come from a verified top-down pipeline.
content.subject: A benchmark-building pipeline, one long kitchen task shown frame by frame with four challenge cards, and a bar chart of trajectory lengths.

lessons.what_to_learn: For a benchmark, stack three tiles: a short construction pipeline with loop-back arrows for quality checks, a numbered filmstrip of one long task with tinted challenge cards linked to the moments that cause them, and a bar chart that makes the headline multiplier visible with one distinct bar and a red note.
lessons.suits: benchmarks or datasets that must show how the data were built, what an example looks like and why it is hard, and one headline number against earlier sets.

evidence: As shown in Fig. 1(c), the average trajectory length reaches 2,972.4 simulation steps—about 6× longer than existing long-horizon manipulation datasets.
A top-down data generation pipeline uses an LLM to produce high-level task instructions and decompose them into subtasks.
(b) A dataset example showing a long, finegrained subtask sequence under dynamically changing visual conditions.

summary: RoboCerebra is a benchmark for System 2 reasoning in long-horizon robotic manipulation, with trajectories about 6 times longer than earlier benchmarks. Figure 1 has three lettered panels. (a) A strip of an Objects Library and six rounded stage boxes with tiny icons, joined by grey block arrows and two green loop-back arrows (regenerate if verification fails, re-annotate if check fails). (b) A filmstrip of ten numbered simulation frames with captions, and four tinted challenge cards (memory exploration, hidden execution, moving objects, observations that conflict with plans) tied to frames by thin coloured lines. (c) A bar chart of average trajectory length for seven benchmarks, where the lilac RoboCerebra bar reaches 2972.4 with a red 6x note.
summary_zh: RoboCerebra 是考察长时程机器人操作中 System 2 推理的基准，轨迹约为已有基准的 6 倍。图 1：(a) 带回环箭头的数据生成流水线，(b) 十帧任务序列与四张挑战卡片，(c) 七个基准的轨迹长度柱状图。
notes: Prior labels kept but regrouped: contribution-mosaic (bento tiles) first, stage-pipeline for panel (a), worked-walkthrough for panel (b), scope-overview for the four challenge cards. The pipeline has six boxes with the Objects Library at its head. Leader lines from cards to frames are thin and pale (orange to frame 1, lavender to frames 4 and 7, green to frame 8); the blue card's line is not clear. The rotated benchmark names under the bars are not in the digest text list.
